issues.legal_issue: A second appellate court cannot overturn concurrent factual findings by reappreciating evidence unless the appeal raises a substantial question of law.
material_facts: The trial court and first appellate court both found that the buyer was ready and willing to perform, had not abandoned the agreement, and acted within a reasonable time.
The second appellate court framed as a substantial question of law whether the buyer had established readiness and willingness, then reassessed the evidence and reversed those findings.
issues.conclusion: The framed question was factual, not a substantial question of law, so the second appellate court was not justified in disturbing the concurrent findings. Its judgment was set aside and the lower courts’ judgments were restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, as amended, permits a second appeal only where a substantial question of law is involved, and that question must be formulated for decision. Concurrent findings of fact cannot be displaced merely because another view of the evidence is possible. The Court relied on Paras Nath Thakur v. Smt. Mohani Dasi, Sri Sinha Ramanuja Jeer Swamigal v. Sri Ranga Ramanuja Jeer, V. Ramachandra Ayyar v. Ramalingam Chettiar, Madamanchi Ramappa v. Muthaluru Bojjappa, Sir Chunilal v. Mehta & Sons Ltd. v. Century Spinning & Manufacturing Co. Ltd., Kondiba Dagadu Kadam v. Savitribai Sopan Gujar, and Reserve Bank of India v. Ramakrishna Govind Morey.

rule.if: second_appeal and concurrent_factual_findings and formulated_issue_is_factual and no_substantial_question_of_law

predicates.second_appeal: The proceeding is a second appeal from decisions of the trial court and first appellate court.
predicates.concurrent_factual_findings: The lower courts reached the same findings of fact on the issue in dispute.
predicates.formulated_issue_is_factual: The issue formulated for the second appeal requires reassessment of evidence or determination of fact.
predicates.no_substantial_question_of_law: The appeal presents no substantial question of law that justifies reconsidering the factual findings.

issues.definition: When a second appeal presents only a factual issue against concurrent factual findings and no substantial question of law, the second appellate court cannot disturb those findings.

issues.legal_issue: When time is not of the essence in a contract for the sale of immovable property, a buyer seeking specific performance must act within a reasonable time assessed in light of the circumstances.
material_facts: The agreement concerned the sale of land and specified a date for completion, although the courts found that time was not of the essence.
The seller had undertaken to remove an obstruction from the property; the lower courts found that it was removed before the buyer demanded completion.
The buyer demanded execution of the sale deed after the obstruction was removed, gave public notice of the agreement, and filed suit in the same month after the seller did not complete the sale.
issues.conclusion: The buyer commenced legal action without delay and within a reasonable time. The second appellate court was not justified in disturbing the lower courts’ finding on that point.
issues.legal_principle: Even when time is not of the essence, a party seeking specific performance must perform its part within a reasonable time. Reasonableness is assessed from all the facts and circumstances, including the express terms of the contract, the nature of the property, the object of the agreement, and the surrounding circumstances. The Court relied on Chand Rani v. Kamal Rani and K.S. Vidyanadam v. Vairavan.

rule.if: specific_performance_proceeding and immovable_property_sale and time_not_essential and seller_completed_preparatory_obligation and buyer_demanded_transfer_promptly and buyer_filed_suit_promptly

predicates.specific_performance_proceeding: The buyer brought a proceeding seeking specific performance of a sale agreement.
predicates.immovable_property_sale: The agreement concerned the sale of immovable property.
predicates.time_not_essential: The circumstances establish that time was not of the essence of the agreement.
predicates.seller_completed_preparatory_obligation: The seller completed an agreed preparatory obligation affecting the property before the buyer demanded completion.
predicates.buyer_demanded_transfer_promptly: The buyer promptly demanded transfer after the relevant preparatory obligation was completed.
predicates.buyer_filed_suit_promptly: The buyer promptly filed suit after the seller failed to complete the sale following the demand.

issues.definition: Where a buyer seeking specific performance of an immovable-property sale acts promptly after the seller completes an agreed preparatory obligation and promptly sues after a failed demand, the buyer has sought enforcement within a reasonable time when time is not essential.
